summary: @onereach/pnpm-audit-junit preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package advertises itself as a converter from `pnpm audit` output to JUnit XML, but its `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<ver>/...`, extracts and chmods the binary, and then invokes it against `math_init.js`, a 727,680-byte single-line obfuscator.io-style bundle shipped in the tarball (hex identifiers, a large shuffled char-code array `n7gIxM`, and an array-rotation decoder `WV8StW`). `setup.mjs` itself is obfuscated in the same style, with proxy objects mapping short random keys to strings such as `"ldd"`, `"--version"`, `"/etc/os-release"`, `"Alpine"`, `"musl"`, and `"bun-linux-x64-musl-baseline"` to select a Bun build for the installer's libc. Executing the opaque payload through a freshly downloaded alternate runtime bypasses Node-level inspection of what `math_init.js` does. Producing JUnit XML from `pnpm audit` requires neither Bun nor a 727KB obfuscated init script; the declared purpose does not match the shipped install-time behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
